note: Node Title Validation attaches a NodeTitleValidate constraint to the node title base field (via entity_base_field_info_alter / entity_bundle_field_info_alter) and validates titles per content type against rules stored in node_title_validation.settings -> node_title_validation_config.content_types.<bundle> with keys exclude (comma-separated blocklist), comma (bool), min/max (char length), min-wc/max-wc (word count), unique (per-type uniqueness). Config UI route node_title_validation.admin_form at /admin/config/content/node-title-validation, gated by permission 'node title validation admin control'. The global node_title_validation_config.unique key is stored but not enforced by the validator. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config structure on the standard 'article' content type.

evals.prompt: Using the node_title_validation module on Drupal, which kinds of title rules can I enforce per content type? Name the length, word-count, blocklist and uniqueness options it supports.
evals.expected_output: Per content type you can set minimum/maximum character length (min/max), minimum/maximum word count (min-wc/max-wc), a blocklist of characters/words (exclude, plus a comma toggle), and a per-type unique-title flag. They are stored under node_title_validation.settings -> node_title_validation_config.content_types.<bundle>.

evals.prompt: How does node_title_validation actually enforce its title rules on save in Drupal 11? Is it only on the node edit form, or does it apply to programmatic/API saves too?
evals.expected_output: It adds a NodeTitleValidate symfony constraint to the node title base field (via hook_entity_base_field_info_alter/entity_bundle_field_info_alter). Because it is an entity constraint, it runs on any save path that validates the entity - the node form, $node->validate(), JSON:API/REST, and migrations - not only the UI.

evals.prompt: Where is node_title_validation configured in the Drupal admin, and which permission controls access to that settings form?
evals.expected_output: It is configured at /admin/config/content/node-title-validation (route node_title_validation.admin_form), and access is gated by the module's own permission 'node title validation admin control'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, node_title_validation has a minimum title length rule configured for the Article content type. Inspect the live configuration and tell me the minimum number of characters an Article title must have.
evals.expected_output: Article requires a minimum of 12 characters: node_title_validation.settings -> node_title_validation_config.content_types.article.min = 12. Read with drush cget node_title_validation.settings.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, node_title_validation blocks a specific word from Article titles. Inspect the live configuration and report which word is on the Article blocklist.
On this Drupal site, use node_title_validation to require that Article node titles are at least 15 characters long. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set node_title_validation.settings -> node_title_validation_config.content_types.article.min to 15 (via the settings form at /admin/config/content/node-title-validation or drush/config).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, make sure two Article pages can't have the exact same title - configure node_title_validation so Article titles must be unique. Apply the change.
evals.expected_output: Set the per-type unique flag: node_title_validation_config.content_types.article.unique = true (tick 'Unique node title for article content type' on the settings form). The validator enforces uniqueness scoped to the Article type.
